An '''individual''', a [[Twi'lek/Legends|Twi'lek]] [[Gender/Legends|male]], was the [[Chief/Legends|head]] of a [[Ryloth Clan|primitive clan]] on [[Ryloth/Legends|Ryloth]]. He was the [[Parent/Legends|father]] of [[Oola/Legends|Oola]], a Twi'lek girl who spent much of her youth dancing due to his unwillingness to educate her. In [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]], a visitor to the clan's village named [[Bib Fortuna/Legends|Bib Fortuna]] saw Oola perform and, rather than purchase the dancer from her father as custom demanded, conspired to kidnap her. Fortuna then [[Slavery/Legends|enslaved]] the girl as a companion for his [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] employer, the [[Crime lord/Legends|crime lord]] [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba Desilijic Tiure]]. Oola's father did not see her again, as she was [[Death/Legends|killed]] by Jabba two [[Standard day/Legends|days]] after arriving at his [[Jabba's Palace/Legends|palace]] on [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]].

==Biography==
Born before [[25 BBY/Legends|25 BBY]],<ref name="Oola's Tale ref 2" /><ref name="Ultimate Alien Anthology" /> a [[Twi'lek/Legends|Twi'lek]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] was a member of the primitive [[Ryloth Clan]]&mdash;a small community of natives from the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] of the [[Ryloth/Legends|same name]]&mdash;where he lived in a village built deep in underground warrens.<ref name="A Time to Mourn, a Time to Dance: Oola's Tale" /> He had a daughter, who was named [[Oola/Legends|Oola]], a word meaning "[[Water/Legends|water]]" in [[Twi'leki/Legends|Twi'leki]].<ref name="Galactic Campaign Guide">''[[Galactic Campaign Guide]]''</ref> By no later than [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]],<ref name="The Essential Atlas">''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' sets [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Return of the Jedi'']] at the start of [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]], so Oola last saw her father four months before the end of [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]].</ref> he became the renowned [[Chief/Legends|chief]] of his eight-hundred-person clan, granting both himself and his family considerable power and influence. Despite this, he provided Oola with little or no formal education, as Twi'lek society held that educating women was a threat to male authority. His daughter instead devoted herself to dancing, which won her dozens of admirers, including a visiting Twi'lek criminal named [[Bib Fortuna/Legends|Bib Fortuna]].<ref name="The Official Star Wars Fact File 96">{{FactFile|96|TWI 19-22|Twi'leks}}</ref> Clan custom gave Oola's [[Parent/Legends|father]] the right to sell her, but Fortuna had doubts that the chief would agree to this, so he abducted the girl during the night.<ref name="A Time to Mourn, a Time to Dance: Oola's Tale" /> Afterward, Fortuna [[Slavery/Legends|enslaved]] Oola at his Ryloth [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggling]] complex, and in [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]] had her taken to the planet [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]] as a gift to his master, [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba Desilijic Tiure]]. The [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] [[Crime lord/Legends|crime lord]] retained the dancer as a concubine in his desert [[Jabba's Palace/Legends|palace]] for two [[Standard day/Legends|days]] before having her [[Death/Legends|killed]], more than four [[Standard month/Legends|months]] since she'd last seen her father and clan.<ref name="Star Wars: The Official Figurine Collection 45" />

==Personality and traits==
Society on Ryloth was oppressive toward Twi'lek females, and Oola's father demonstrated this widespread bigotry by restricting her education.<ref name="The Official Star Wars Fact File 96" /> Bib Fortuna believed that he might have been unwilling to subject his daughter to a life of slavery, however.<ref name="Star Wars: The Official Figurine Collection 45" /> Even though Oola's father followed the laws and rules of not educating his daughter he refused to obey the custom of letting Fortuna take his daughter as a slave. Oola's father gave her the opportunity to take classes at a great dance school, an opportunity his daughter would turn down for a chance of a new life in Jabba's Palace.

==Behind the scenes==
The Twi'lek chief was first mentioned in the [[1990]] [[West End Games]] sourcebook ''[[Galaxy Guide 5: Return of the Jedi]]''. To date, he has only received mentions in various sources detailing Oola's backstory.
